question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births registered in Taiwan in September 2026, as reported in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics.

target.what: Number of live births registered in Taiwan (Republic of China) during September 2026, as counted in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics (births registered in the month, by month of registration/occurrence as published in the MOI 'Household Registration Statistics
target.publisher: Ministry of the Interior (內政部), Department of Household Registration (戶政司), Taiwan
target.cadence: Monthly, typically released in the following month (preliminary monthly bulletin ~mid-following-month; fuller statistics later)
target.caveats: Target period is future/incomplete relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff: September 2026 has not yet occurred, so this is a forecast. Definitional issues: (1) 'registered births' are counted by registration date, not birth date, so late registration can shift counts across months; (2) MOI monthly figure

candidates.hypothesis: September registered births in recent years, plus the most recent months published before the cutoff (e.g., Jan–Jul 2026), anchor a trend-plus-seasonality forecast; September typically shows a modest seasonal pattern relative to adjacent months. Target = recent monthly level × September seasonal factor × trend adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: MOI monthly birth counts for September 2019–2025 and all months of 2025 and Jan–Jul/Aug 2026; ideally the same-month year-over-year ratios and the month-of-year seasonal index. Minimum: last 3 Septembers and the latest 6–12 monthly values before cutoff.

directions.hypothesis: The September seasonal adjustment divisor (analogous to p67–p69 for Oct/Nov/Dec) is not directly published in the kept data; only the September 2025 unadjusted and seasonally adjusted rates (p62/p63) allow an inference. assumptions.name: September 2026 seasonal factor relative to the 2026 Jan–Jul average monthly level
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 registered births (8,603, p46/p174) were about 1.6% above the 2025 Jan–Jul average (8,433+8,968+8,939+8,464+8,603 over 5 months ≈ 8,681; 8,603/8,681 ≈ 0.99), and the published September 2025 seasonal adjustment implies September is slightly above the seasonally adjusted level (4.49/4.42 ≈ 1.016). assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the 2026 Jan–Jul average monthly registered births to a September level; assumes the September seasonal pattern in 2026 resembles 2025 and earlier years.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 has an unusually large registration backlog or a policy/administrative shift that moves births into or out of September.

assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale September 2025 registered births (p46/p174) to September 2026; assumes the 2026 year-on-year decline in September is similar to the recent July 2026 decline.

This means a September registration-month count mixes September and late-August/early-September occurrences, so occurrence-based routes need a lag conversion.

Mid-Autumn/Teachers' Day 4-day holiday 25–28 September 2026 confirmed by two sources; registration offices closed on those days, a minor downward shift in registrations within the month (mostly recovered in-month).

assumptions.applies_when: The within-year seasonal shape of 2026 resembles 2024–2025 and the Jan–Jul average is a valid base level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong September-specific registration surge or slump in 2026.

methods.label: m1

p144.role: May 2026 registered live births in Taiwan (monthly level)

p145.role: June 2026 registered live births in Taiwan (monthly level)

p118.role: July 2026 registered live births in Taiwan (monthly level)

a1.role: September seasonal factor relative to the May–July 2026 average monthly level

methods.rationale: Level-plus-seasonality route: the most recent three observed months (May–July 2026) give the current monthly level, and a1 applies the small September seasonal adjustment. Shared dependency: all three level points come from the same MOI release, so their errors are correlated; the interval is dominated by a1 and by the risk that August–September diverge from the May–July level.

methods.label: m2

p46.role: September 2025 registered live births in Taiwan (same calendar month, prior year)

a2.role: year-on-year change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025 registered births

methods.rationale: Year-on-year route: September 2025 registered births (8,603) scaled by the 2026-vs-2025 change factor. The factor is anchored on the observed Jan–Jul 2026 decline (−15.6%) and the moderating July decline (−11.6%). Failure mode: if the 2026 decline re-steepens or the 2025 September base was itself distorted by registration timing, the factor is wrong.

weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

kept.name: September 2026 seasonal factor relative to the 2026 May–July average monthly level
kept.rationale: 2023 divisors put September near neutral (0.987) and the 2025 unadjusted/SA September rates imply a divisor of roughly 0.99–1.02; September is not a strong seasonal month in Taiwan. A factor centred at 1.0 with a ±7–8% band reflects the small and uncertain seasonal signal plus the 4-day late-Septemb
kept.applies_when: The May–July 2026 average is a fair proxy for the underlying late-2026 monthly level and no large registration-timing shift occurs.
kept.falsified_by: A published September seasonal divisor far from 1.0, or evidence that the 2026 holiday closure shifted a large share of registrations into October.

kept.name: Year-on-year change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025 registered births
kept.rationale: Jan–Jul 2026 births are 54,250 vs 64,314 a year earlier (−15.6%, p121/p422); July alone was −11.6% (p147/p321). The decline has been moderating through spring–summer (May 6,832, June 7,324, July 7,906), so a September YoY factor somewhat milder than the year-to-date −15.6% but still clearly negative
kept.applies_when: The moderating month-on-month recovery seen in May–July 2026 continues into September rather than reversing.
kept.falsified_by: An August 2026 figure showing a renewed steep drop (e.g. below ~7,000) or a sharp rebound above ~8,500.

kept.name: Ratio of September 2026 registered births to the 2026 Jan–Jul monthly average
kept.rationale: In 2025 September (8,603) was 0.96 of the Jan–Jul 2025 monthly average (9,188); in 2024 September (11,169) was about 1.0 of the Jan–Jul average. September is close to the annual mean, so a ratio near 1 with a modest band is justified; the slight upward tilt reflects the May–July 2026 recovery.
kept.applies_when: The within-year seasonal shape of 2026 resembles 2024–2025 and the Jan–Jul average is a valid base level.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong September-specific registration surge or slump in 2026.

kept.name: Number of months in the January–July 2026 cumulative window
kept.rationale: Calendar constant: the Jan–Jul cumulative (p421) spans exactly seven months, so dividing by it gives the monthly average. Fixed, not uncertain.
kept.applies_when: Used only to convert the Jan–Jul cumulative to a monthly average.
kept.falsified_by: Nothing; it is a calendar fact.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
